text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS

RZECZPOSPOLITA - Around 186,000 hectares of land are still flooded in southern Poland and 43,000 inhabitants of the areas stay away from homes, the spokesman for the flood crisis committee Krzysztof Pomes said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The opposition left-wing Union of Labour (UP) expects to get more than 10 percent of support in the parlaimentary elections in September, the party's elections committee chairman Artur Smolko said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's corporate sector invested 14.2 billion zlotys in development from January to May 1997 showing a 27 percent growth compared with the same period last year, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Gdansk Transport Company construction firm will receive a licence to build the Gdansk-Torun stretch of the A1 motrway in northern Poland, the Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said.

- Penalties for violations of stock market regulations accounted for the brunt of the Polish Securites Commission revenues amounting to 1.75 million in 1996, a report by the Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) said. The chamber's inspectors were satisfied with the bourse's financial arrangements.

- Poland's banking sector's credit and deposit growth slowed down in the second quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year, a report by the Infomarket Poznan market research agency showed.
- The listed Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej (BWR) has appointed Aldona Czekaj to join the bank's board. Czekaj is the president of Bank Secesyjny to be integrated shortly with BWR.

- The board of the Polskie Towarzystwo Reasekuracyjne (PTR) reinsurance firm has assigned 40,000 shares to six new investors including Altra, BWR bank, Hogson, AS Motors, AmerBank and Nafta Polska. The new investors will increase the firm's share capital to 105.1 million zlotys from 65 million zlotys, PTR said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's road accidents bring annual losses of 14 billion zlotysm, an equivalent of more than 10 percent of the national budget, a police report said.
- Combined net assets of Poland's mutual funds totalled 1.956 billion zlotys in June 1997, four million zloty less than in May, the funds' reports showed.
- Poland's private fuel distributors expect fuel shoratges due to growing oil prices on world markets and costly dollar, which make imports unprofitable, the Reflex brokerage in Lodz said.
- Alcohol production in 1996 declined to 124 million litres from 154 million litres the year before mainly as a result of large scale bootlegging from Russia, a report by the trade ministry said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Half of the GSM mobile telephone subscribers are independant businesspeople and 20 percent of the subscribers are female while the average age of the mobile users is decreasing, a report by the Era GSM operator said.
ZYCIE
- The cabinet will decide about the privatisation of Poland's biggest insurance firm, the state-owned PZU SA, following publication of a report by the NIK auduting chamber, a source said.
